title: How Sink Drainage Works: Traps, Vents, and Gravity
description: A sink drainage system relies on gravity and atmospheric pressure to remove wastewater safely and effectively. At the heart of this system is the P-trap, a curved section of pipe that holds a water seal to block dangerous sewer gases from entering the living space. Downstream of the trap, the drainage pipe connects to a vent stack, which introduces air into the system to prevent negative pressure from siphoning the water out of the trap. Understanding how gravity flow and venting work together ensures that water drains smoothly without gurgling, backing up, or allowing odors through the fixture opening.
